A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SHAP zero and contain readable main text, mathematics, figures, tables and appendices. Shared methods and experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial restructuring and an expanded application scope.

before.justification: v2 reports original SHAP zero evaluations on TIGER and inDelphi, including prediction accuracy, attribution comparisons, runtimes and biological interaction analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds Tranception protein-fitness experiments, RNA encoding-sensitivity results and baseline convergence analyses.

M1.justification: The sparse-Fourier sketch, conversion to a Möbius transform around each query, and SHAP/Faith-Shap summations are retained. The q-ary formulation already existed in v2; expanded recovery details and protein evaluation do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v3 retains TIGER and inDelphi and adds GFP protein-fitness explanations using Tranception over a 20-amino-acid alphabet and ten variable sites. Appendix A.3 also evaluates an RNA-splicing model with nine-base inputs, adding a distinct biological task.

E2.justification: The retained experiments preserve their linear/pairwise predictors, KernelSHAP, SHAP-IQ, FastSHAP and TIGER-only DeepSHAP comparisons. The new Tranception comparisons reuse KernelSHAP, SHAP-IQ and FastSHAP; newly cited attribution methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include 200 generated GFP variants with up to five mutations, a 79-sequence background, and four RNA encodings evaluated on 10,000 sequences. For retained tasks, v3 replaces the reported visual-convergence tuning rules with explicit search grids and R2 thresholds, while retaining the selected background sizes and SHAP-IQ budgets.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds an encoding-sensitivity analysis, and Figure 10 adds quantitative convergence analyses over background sizes and evaluation budgets. v2 described visual convergence without presenting these analyses. v3 also adds a protein interaction case study examining context-dependent residue effects.

E5.justification: v3 adds uncertainty bands for R2 convergence in Figure 10 and plus/minus summaries across encoding experiments in Appendix A.3. These describe variation across sequences or encodings; repeated-seed run counts and the precise statistical meaning of the bands remain unspecified.

E6.justification: New Tranception results report agreement correlations of 0.97 with KernelSHAP and 0.61 with SHAP-IQ, with amortized runtimes of 5.2 versus 17.7 and 38.1 minutes. Table 1 adds RNA reconstruction R2 values of 0.77–0.80. Existing benchmark values in Figures 2–3 and the six supplementary result tables are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds explicit Fourier aliasing and bin-detection formulas, a Gaussian-noise assumption and an encoding-invariance argument. The central Fourier–Möbius–SHAP identities, proofs and complexity bounds remain from v2 Section 9, principally reorganized into Section 3 and Appendix C.

C1.justification: The central claims of Fourier-based amortization, near-zero marginal explanation cost and efficient interaction discovery remain. The abstract and contribution list broaden the demonstrated scope from genomic models to biological sequence models, explicitly adding protein fitness and epistatic interactions.

C2.justification: v3 adds protein-residue interpretations, a biophysical rationale for sparsity, sampling-cost discussion and an encoding-robustness interpretation. It explains Tranception's attribution differences through marginalization distributions and explicitly acknowledges that SHAP zero and KernelSHAP estimate different quantities. The proposed TreeSHAP integration discussion is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds a query-count formula, expanded hardware and tuning information, and detailed Tranception model and sequence-generation settings. v3 also changes the stated code link to an anonymous repository and omits v2's data-availability section, including its explicit figshare accession. This establishes changed access documentation, not whether resources remain available.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands protein-model, epistasis and RNA-splicing references and discusses additional amortized attribution research, including Stochastic Amortization and Fourier-based SHAP approximation. Section 5 newly distinguishes SHAP zero from binary-input alternatives, while the explicit TreeSHAP integration positioning disappears.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. v2's Results/Discussion/Methods organization becomes Background, Algorithm, Experiments, Discussion and Conclusion, with theoretical development and implementation material redistributed across the main text and Appendices A–E.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redrawn, and v3 adds Figures 4, 9 and 10 plus Tables 1 and 8–10. Existing figures are restyled; supplementary Figures S1–S4 become Figures 5–8 and Tables S1–S6 become Tables 2–7. Title, typography, table spacing and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: The new protein case study, quantitative convergence checks and fuller algorithm explanation improve evidential support and readability. The gain is tempered by very small SHAP-IQ convergence subsets, encoding robustness tested only under four cyclic relabelings, and removal of v2's explicit data-repository disclosure.
